summary_paragraph: The patient was re-admitted due to a thrombosed left upper extremity AV graft, preventing dialysis access. A fistulogram and thrombectomy were attempted but were unsuccessful due to persistent stenosis in the graft. A temporary dialysis catheter was placed in the left internal jugular vein and later converted to a tunneled catheter. The patient received one dialysis session during admission and was stabilized. Chronic abdominal and left breast wounds were assessed; no abscess was found, and wound care was optimized for home management. The transplant surgery team will contact the patient to schedule outpatient graft repair. She was discharged home with visiting nurse services for wound care and instructions to resume regular dialysis through the tunneled catheter.
problems: Thrombosed left upper extremity AV graft
